news.126: Option to draw offcut cuts (simple or detailed), and options grouped under “Method”. Origin in the centre or mid-edge: more compact group of parts.
news.125: Faster free rotation, no extra panel depending on the chosen origin, smaller origin marker that is always fully visible.
news.124: Fix: parts could overlap with the origin in the centre. Grouping around the origin never needs more panels.
news.123: Option to export the panel outline with the parts (on its own layer). Parts are grouped in a compact block around the chosen origin.
dl.board: Include the panel outline in exports
news.122: Safer SVG import: only the file’s geometry is kept. Automated tests and reorganised code.

news.111: List of what’s new in the settings.
news.110: Part names and layers, sorting, LightBurn, VectorCraft, HPGL and SVGZ import, per-part scale and duplication.
news.109: New logo: the N straight on the blue background.
news.108: Free rotation in 5° steps, rotation setting for all parts, SVG import fixed.
news.107: The page loads from the network when online, so icons stay up to date.
news.106: Icons renamed to force an update on devices.
news.105: New logo, drawn Nestor title, blueprint-style background and translated title block.
news.112: Full version history and a button to report a bug on GitHub.
news.100: First version: nesting DXF, SVG and AI parts on sheets, SVG and DXF export, installable app in 45 languages.
bug.title: A problem?
bug.hint: Opens a report on GitHub, already filled in with technical details (GitHub account needed, the report is public). Your file is never sent: attach it yourself if you want.
news.113: New PolyForm Perimeter license: free use for everyone, including at work, but no resale or competing copies. Name and logo reserved.
origin.title: Placement point (machine zero)
origin.hint: Parts are grouped from this point, and it is the zero of the exported files.
news.120: Portrait sheets, import of several files and adding to the current job, choice of the origin (machine zero).
calc.many: {n} parts to place: this may take a while.
news.121: Quantities are no longer capped at 500, oversized parts are reported right away, and a Cancel button appears during a long calculation.
news.1101: Kits are now called groups. New “Number of groups” choice to place exactly the number you want; if room runs out, Nestor tells you how many are complete.
news.1100: Projects in your own folder: USB stick, iCloud, Dropbox… (Chrome and Edge on a computer). Several kits, each with its own name. Clearer “Fill as much as possible”. Collapsible blocks with a summary. Anonymous export counter, can be turned off in Settings.
news.199: Kits: tick “Kit” on the parts of one object, and Nestor fills a sheet with as many whole objects as possible. In fixed direction, ↺ and ↻ turn a part a quarter turn. New “Free (1°)” rotation. Guide: previous and next topic, ← → keys, two new topics.
news.198: New “Guide” button at the top: 12 short topics by category, from importing to cost, with a search and “Show me in the app” to find the right place. The “?” next to a block’s title opens its topic.
news.197: Sheets are numbered when there are several, with a small arrow to give them a name. “Fill” now targets a sheet row (its number or name): fill its last sheet in the plan, all its sheets, or a new one. Projects: a project saved with an imported file before 1.9.6 opens again, and opening a project no longer fails when the plan shown before had more parts.
news.196: Lock: each sheet of the plan can be locked; its parts no longer move, and new parts (another file, a higher quantity) go into its gaps first. Fill: a part can fill everything left on the chosen sheet, or a new sheet. Projects: a project with an imported file opens again.
news.195: Fixes after a full review: the Projects, Settings and Shortcuts windows keep the keyboard inside and give it back to the right button when they close; a sheet with no size is clearly flagged; a file in another format (an image, for example) is reported as “unrecognised format”; a material with a zero or negative size is no longer saved silently; “Estimated cutting” no longer mentions the cutter when nothing is placed.
news.194: Import: when the parts of a drawing interlock, each inner line stays on its own part (it is no longer carried off by the neighbouring part).
news.193: Nesting: a part that doesn’t fit is flagged in red in the parts list, with the reason, and the red message takes you to it. “Origin” becomes “Placement point”. The chosen material puts its format on a sheet row, and “Add an offcut” puts offcuts in front. Saw: choose the direction of the first cuts. “Whole plan as DXF” downloads one DXF per sheet. Cost: separate machine and labour rates, started hours charged as whole hours if you want, offcuts at 0 by default. Milling: your spindle speeds are explained. Milling and Laser: the recommended settings no longer follow scrolling. Laser: manufacturer thicknesses are explained under the field. AI import: names given to paths in Illustrator are used for the parts.
news.192: Milling: “Maximum depth of cut” and “Passes to make” are explained in plain words, and a minimum margin based on the bit (Ø + 1 mm) joins the minimum gap between parts. Tabs in a new order: Nesting, Milling, Laser, Materials, Notebook, Cost.
news.191: Saw cutting order: the large offcut comes off in a single cut instead of being sliced into strips, and the numbers go where they hide neither the parts nor other numbers (smaller in the PDF).
news.190: Parts entered by hand (or pasted from a spreadsheet), saw cutting order for the Rectangles method (with your blade thickness), your own laser materials and values, indicative values from Thunder Laser and GWK (plywood, MDF, acrylic, cardboard, leather…), and no more offcut lines along the margins.
news.181: On phones, the Projects and Settings buttons now sit below the logo instead of covering it.
news.180: New Laser tab (your machines, starting point from the Trotec books, test grid), printable PDF under each panel or for the whole plan, part numbers to engrave, saved projects (Projects button) and keyboard shortcuts (? key).
news.170: New Cost tab (cost price of the plan: material, offcut, machine, per part) and Materials tab (library of your boards with their price). The chosen material is the same in Nesting, Milling and Cost.
news.160: New Notebook tab to keep your proven settings (milling, laser, other), with backup to a file. Files are exported in inches when the app is in inches. Nesting: parts no longer slide away from the edge to interlock their tabs.
news.150: Nesting: estimated cutting time and spacing from the cutter. Milling: formula reminder. Settings: metric or imperial units (decimal or fractional inches), sizes never change.
news.141: Milling: V-bit for engraving, cutter types as illustrated cards, 24 more woods and materials (OSB, Dibond, ABS, fibreglass, robinia…), roughing / finishing choice removed. Settings: choose light or dark theme.
news.140: New Milling tab: spindle speed, feed rate and depth of cut for your cutter, material and machine.
news.130: Lighter app (only one language loaded) and better protected (page security policy, oversized SVGZ files rejected). Clear message for a damaged PDF. Code reorganised and better tested. Fix: right after an update, the app could keep part of the old version (offcut cuts had no effect on iPhone). PDF/AI reader updated (pdf.js 6.5).

mill.rule: Chip load {c} {u} per flute (Ø / {k}), depth {f} × Ø.
mill.ruleVBit: Chip load {c} {u} per flute (cutting width / {k}), engraved in one pass.
mill.prudent: Cautious starting values: listen to the machine and adjust. On a less rigid machine or without dust extraction, reduce the depth.
mill.invalid: Enter the cutter diameter and number of flutes.
mill.invalidVBit: Enter the diameter, number of flutes, angle (between 1 and 179°) and engraving depth.
mill.noteMax: Your spindle tops out at {n} rpm: the feed is reduced to keep the same chip load.
mill.noteMin: Your spindle cannot go below {n} rpm: the feed is increased to keep the same chip load.
mill.noteFeedMax: Your machine cannot feed faster than {n} {u}/min: the spindle speed is lowered to keep the same chip load.
mill.noteThinChip: Even at your spindle’s lowest speed, you would need to feed faster than {n} {u}/min: the chip will be thinner than advised and the cutter may heat up. A cutter with fewer flutes helps.
mill.noteMelt: Plastic that melts: prefer a single-flute cutter, which makes a bigger chip.
mill.noteDowncut: Downcut spiral: chips stay in the groove. If it heats up, reduce the depth.
mill.noteCompression: Compression: the first pass must be deeper than the upcut part of the cutter.
mill.noteVBit: V-bit: at {e} {u} deep it cuts {d} {u} wide. Settings are calculated on that width.
mill.noteVBitDeep: Deeper than the conical tip: the cutter cuts its full width ({d} {u}).
res.timeNote: Estimate: only the outer contour of each part, with the feed and passes from the Milling tab, without rapid moves, plunges or inner holes.
res.timeNoThickness: enter the thickness in the Milling tab
res.timeNone: set the cutter in the Milling tab
mill.thVc: The speed at which the cutting edge moves through the material, in m/min. The harder the material, the lower it is.
mill.thN: N in rpm, Vc in m/min, Ø (cutter diameter) in mm.
mill.thFz: The thickness each flute removes, a fraction of the diameter depending on the material. Too thin and the cutter rubs and heats; too thick and it strains and may break.
mill.thVf: Z: number of flutes. Vf in mm/min.
mill.thAp: K depends on the material. The thickness to cut is split into equal passes.
mill.thV: p: engraving depth. This cutting width replaces Ø in the formulas.
mill.thLimits: The chip load is always kept: if the spindle cannot turn fast enough, the feed drops; if the machine cannot feed fast enough, the speed drops.
mill.thGap: At least twice the diameter plus a margin m of material, otherwise the cutter paths meet and the part can move.
mill.thMetric: Calculated in millimetres, converted for display.
mill.thSources: Sources: id-conception.fr (chip and depth from the diameter), cncfraises.fr (cutting speed), Vectric documentation (spacing between parts).

lz.title: Laser settings
lz.gridHint: 16 squares: 4 powers × 4 speeds around the starting point, one colour per square. Give each colour the power and speed written next to it, run the grid on an offcut and keep the best square.
lz.prudent: Starting values to test on an offcut. Never leave a laser unattended.
lz.thSource: The starting values come from the parameter books published by Trotec for its 60, 80 and 120 W CO2 lasers (2-inch lens, air assist, grid table). They are used as published, without correction.
lz.thEnergy: P is the machine power (W), p the power setting (%), v the speed setting. E tells how much energy each millimetre of line receives: that is what cuts or marks the material.
lz.thPower: For a power with no book (100 W, 40 W…), E is taken between the two neighbouring books, or from the nearest one, then the speed is recalculated. For engraving, the speed stays and the power changes.
lz.thThickness: For an unpublished thickness, the speed is scaled in proportion to the nearest published thickness. On thick stock, several passes are often better: test it.
lz.thSpeed: Trotec machines set speed in %; other machines often in mm/s. Nestor converts using the maximum speed of the Speedy 360. This is the least reliable conversion: use the test grid.
lz.addFirst: Add your machine (name, type, power) to see the starting point.

mill.maxPassSub: {u} · from the bit and the material
mill.passPlan: {t} {u} ÷ max depth {m} {u} → {p} equal passes of {d} {u}. Nestor splits the thickness into equal passes, none deeper than the maximum.
panel.toolIntro: From the {d} {u} bit in the Milling tab:
mill.spindleFrom: Where these values come from: 6,000–24,000 rpm is the most common range for CNC spindles (for example a 2.2 kW water-cooled spindle). It isn’t necessarily your machine.
mill.spindleEffect: What they change: Nestor never suggests a speed outside them. If the calculation asks for more than the maximum, the speed is capped and the feed lowered to match, to keep the same chip (and the reverse below the minimum).
mill.spindleWhere: To set yours: read them on the spindle’s plate, in your router’s manual (often 10,000–30,000 rpm), or in the VFD settings (2-pole spindle: rpm = frequency × 60, so 400 Hz = 24,000 rpm).

guide.start.title: Your first plan in 2 minutes
guide.start.intro: Nestor places your parts on sheets while wasting as little material as possible, then gives you the files for the machine.
guide.start.s1: In Nesting, import your drawing (DXF, SVG, AI or PDF), or type your parts with “Enter by hand”.
guide.start.s2: Enter the size of your sheets and the spacing between parts (at least your cutter’s diameter).
guide.start.s3: The plan is calculated on its own: check how many parts are placed and how much is left as waste.
guide.start.s4: Download the DXF, SVG or PDF of each sheet, or the whole plan at once.
guide.start.tip: Your files stay on your computer: only an anonymous export counter goes over the internet (topic “Your data”).
guide.import.title: Importing parts
guide.import.intro: Each closed outline in your drawing becomes a part; what is inside it (engraving, holes) goes with it.
guide.import.s1: Drag one or more files into the import area, or tap it to choose them.
guide.import.s2: Check the drawing size shown under the file name; if it is wrong, change “File units”.
guide.import.s3: In the parts list, set the quantity, rotation and scale of each one.
guide.import.s4: “Add files” adds to the current work without erasing what is already there.
guide.import.tip: Names given to paths in Illustrator, or to layers, become the names of the parts.
guide.panels.title: Sheets and offcuts
guide.panels.intro: Sheets are used in the order of the list: put your offcuts first to use them up first.
guide.panels.s1: Choose a material from your library: its format fills the “Material format” row.
guide.panels.s2: “Add an offcut” puts an offcut in front: give it its size and stock.
guide.panels.s3: With several rows, the small arrow next to the number lets you name each sheet.
guide.panels.s4: The placement point chooses the corner where parts gather; it is also the zero of exported files.
guide.panels.tip: Empty stock = unlimited. A part that doesn’t fit is marked in red in the list, with the reason.
guide.lock.title: Lock and fill
guide.lock.intro: Keep a sheet as it is and fill its gaps with other parts, or fill an offcut with a single part.
guide.lock.s1: Calculate your plan, then click “Lock” on the sheet you like: its parts will no longer move.
guide.lock.s2: Add a file or raise a quantity: new parts go into the gaps of locked sheets first.
guide.lock.s3: To fill: in a part’s quantity list, choose “Fill as much as possible”, then the sheet and “the last sheet”, “all sheets” or “a new sheet”.
guide.lock.tip: While a sheet is locked, the spacing, the margin and the size of its row are greyed out.
guide.saw.title: Saw: straight cuts
guide.saw.intro: For cutting with a saw: the Rectangles method only places parts that can be cut out with straight cuts, from edge to edge.
guide.saw.s2: Tick “Saw cutting order”: cuts are numbered on each sheet, with their list underneath.
guide.saw.s3: Enter the “Blade thickness”: it is removed after each cut. If the spacing between parts is smaller, a link offers to fix it.
guide.saw.s4: “First cuts”: best choice, along the length or across the width first.
guide.saw.tip: Each cut goes from one edge of the piece to the other, measured from its left or top edge. The list is also in the PDF.
guide.export.title: Exporting and printing
guide.export.intro: Each sheet of the plan downloads as DXF or SVG for the machine, or as PDF for the workshop.
guide.export.s1: Under each sheet: “Download DXF”, “Download SVG” or “Download PDF”.
guide.export.s2: Under the plan: “Whole plan as DXF” (one file per sheet) or “Whole plan as PDF” (with a summary page).
guide.export.s3: Options: “Include the panel outline in exports” and “Engrave part numbers”, each on its own layer.
guide.export.s4: “Offcut cuts” adds straight lines to recover offcuts with a saw.
guide.export.tip: Files are in mm (in inches if you chose that in Settings), with the zero on the placement point. Original layers and colours are kept.
guide.mill.title: Milling settings
guide.mill.intro: Nestor suggests a starting spindle speed, feed and passes for your cutter, your material and your machine.
guide.mill.s1: Choose the cutter type, then its diameter and number of flutes.
guide.mill.s2: Choose a material family, or “Choose a specific material” (oak, MDF, aluminium…).
guide.mill.s3: Enter your spindle’s minimum and maximum speeds, the max feed and the thickness to cut.
guide.mill.s4: Read the “Suggested settings”; “Understanding the calculation” explains each formula.
guide.mill.tip: These are cautious starting values: test on an offcut. The cutter diameter is also used to suggest the minimum spacing between parts.
guide.laser.title: Laser settings
guide.laser.intro: A starting point for cutting or engraving a material, based on the tables published by Trotec, Thunder Laser and GWK Laser.
guide.laser.s1: In “My machines”, “Add” your machine: laser type and power in watts.
guide.laser.s2: Choose the material, the operation and the thickness: the starting settings appear.
guide.laser.s3: After your tests, “Edit these values” saves them for this machine; “New material” adds your own materials.
guide.laser.s4: “Test grid”: 16 power × speed squares, as SVG or DXF, to run on an offcut.
guide.laser.tip: Never leave a laser unattended. Above 10 mm, the laser is only for engraving.
guide.notebook.title: Settings notebook
guide.notebook.intro: Keep the settings that worked, to find them again next time.
guide.notebook.s1: In Milling or Laser, “Keep in the notebook” saves the values shown.
guide.notebook.s2: Correct the values you really used, add a note and a result: “✓ Approved” or “⚠ To review”.
guide.notebook.s3: Find a setting with the search, or filter by process and by machine.
guide.notebook.s4: “Export” saves the notebook to a file; “Import” loads it on another computer.
guide.notebook.tip: “Open in Milling” puts a milling setting back into the Milling tab.
guide.materials.title: Materials and prices
guide.materials.intro: Your library of usual sheets, with their prices. The material chosen for the project is used everywhere: Nesting, Milling and Cost.
guide.materials.s1: “Add a material”: name, milling material, thickness, size and price of the sheet.
guide.materials.s2: “Use” puts it in the project: it fills the sheet size, sets up milling and gives the price in Cost.
guide.materials.s3: The “Price per area” is calculated so you can compare your sheets.
guide.materials.s4: “Export” saves the library to a file; “Import” loads it on another computer.
guide.materials.tip: The project material can also be chosen from the “Material” list in the other tabs.
guide.cost.title: Cost of the plan
guide.cost.intro: The cost price of the plan: material, machine, labour, and the cost of each part.
guide.cost.s1: First calculate a plan in Nesting, then choose the material or type the sheet price.
guide.cost.s2: “Last board”: counted in full, or only the part used (the offcut goes back to stock).
guide.cost.s3: Enter the machine and labour hourly rates and the preparation time; the cutting time comes from the plan.
guide.cost.s4: Read the total cost price and the cost per part, shared out by area.
guide.cost.tip: An offcut added to the sheets counts as 0: it is already paid for. All of this is an estimate.
guide.projects.title: Projects
guide.projects.intro: A project keeps everything: imported files, parts, sheets, locks, options, material and settings.
guide.projects.s1: Click “Projects” at the top, give a name, then “Save” (or Ctrl+S, ⌘+S on Mac).
guide.projects.s2: In “This browser”, “Open” picks a project up exactly as you left it.
guide.projects.s3: “Export the file” gives a .nestor file, to reopen on another computer with “Import a file”.
guide.projects.s4: “New project” starts from scratch; Nestor warns you if the current project isn’t saved.
guide.projects.tip: “This browser” keeps projects on this device only: to take them along, use “My folder” or “Export the file”.
guide.folder.title: Projects on your USB stick or cloud
guide.folder.intro: Keep your projects in a folder of your own: a USB stick, iCloud Drive, Dropbox, Nextcloud… You find them on any computer.
guide.folder.s1: Open “Projects”, tab “My folder”, then “Choose a folder” (on your stick or in your cloud folder).
guide.folder.s2: “Save” (or Ctrl+S) writes a .nestor file named after the project; “Save a copy” makes a second one without overwriting.
guide.folder.s3: The list shows the folder’s projects, newest first: “Open” picks one up. On each visit, the browser asks again for access to the folder.
guide.folder.s4: Stick unplugged? Nestor tells you: plug it back in, or “Change folder”. “Forget this folder” deletes no file.
guide.folder.tip: Works in Chrome and Edge on a computer. Elsewhere (Safari, Firefox, phone): “Export the file” to save it wherever you like, “Import a file” to reopen it.
kit.noRoom: No room for a whole group.
guide.rotation.title: Rotating parts
guide.rotation.intro: For each part, you choose how Nestor is allowed to turn it to fit it better.
guide.rotation.s1: “Fixed direction”: the part keeps its direction (wood grain, veneer, engraving); it can only turn half a turn.
guide.rotation.s2: In fixed direction, ↺ and ↻ turn the part a quarter turn: its size is swapped and the angle is shown next to it.
guide.rotation.s3: “Quarter turns” tries the four quarter turns; “Free (5°)” tries every angle in 5° steps.
guide.rotation.s4: “Free (1°)” tries every angle in 1° steps: the most precise for angled parts, but the slowest.
guide.rotation.tip: “Rotation for all parts”, at the top of the list, sets all parts at once.
guide.kit.title: Groups: whole objects
guide.kit.intro: A group is the parts of one object (the sides of a box…). Nestor places as many whole groups as possible, never half a group.
guide.kit.s1: On a part’s row, in the “No group” list, choose “+ New group”: the Groups block appears, give the group a name.
guide.kit.s2: Put each part of the object in this group with the same list: their quantity becomes the quantity per group.
guide.kit.s3: In the Groups block, choose “A single group”, “Number of groups” (type the number) or “Fill as much as possible” then the sheet: the number of complete groups is shown.
guide.kit.s4: Several objects? One group per object: they are placed in the block’s order. Small parts outside groups set to “Fill as much as possible” go into the gaps.
guide.kit.tip: Calculation order: locked sheets, normal parts and counted groups, groups set to “Fill as much as possible”, then filling parts. When filling, the space left stays free.
set.statsHint: Only the format and Nestor’s version go to its counter, to know which exports are used. Never your files, your parts or anything that identifies you.
guide.privacy.title: Your data
guide.privacy.intro: Nestor runs in your browser: your drawings never leave your computer.
guide.privacy.s1: Imported files, parts, sheets and projects stay in this browser, or wherever you save them.
guide.privacy.s2: With each export, an anonymous counter receives only the format (DXF, SVG, PDF…) and Nestor’s version.
guide.privacy.s3: No cookie, no IP address recorded, no file or project name: there is no way to know who exported what.
guide.privacy.s4: To turn it off: Settings, untick “Count my exports, anonymously”.
guide.privacy.tip: The counter is only used to know which formats matter, to improve Nestor.
